plain_english_title: Heart & Vascular Regulations (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.100–4.104): Pre-1998, 1998–2021 Ejection Fraction & Post-2021 METs
what_this_means: VA's cardiovascular rating schedule (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.100–4.104) spans three distinct historical eras that every Veteran with heart disease—especially Agent Orange / Nehmer Ischemic Heart Disease (Diagnostic Code 7005)—should understand: (1) before January 12, 1998, qualitative congestive heart failure, angina, and 'more than light manual labor' rules; (2) from January 12, 1998 through November 13, 2021 (62 FR 65207; § 4.100 added October 6, 2006), BOTH exercise workload in METs AND standalone Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (LVEF < 30% = 100%; LVEF 30%–50% = 60%) plus ECG/X-ray/echocardiogram heart enlargement (30%); and (3) effective November 14, 2021 (86 FR 54089, corrected November 9 and November 29, 2021), a unified General Rating Formula for Diseases of the Heart centered on METs workload and echocardiogram/MUGA/MRI hypertrophy (removing standalone LVEF for newly filed claims while protecting existing ratings).
record_clues: A heart rating decision between January 12, 1998 and November 13, 2021—or a Nehmer retroactive award covering those years—that assigned 10% or 30% based on METs while overlooking an echocardiogram or MUGA scan showing Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (LVEF) of 30%–50% (60%) or under 30% (100%), or ECG/X-ray cardiac hypertrophy (30%).
A heart claim pending across November 14, 2021 where VA failed to award a higher staged rating for the pre-November 14, 2021 period based on LVEF or ECG/X-ray hypertrophy.

Peripheral Arterial Disease (Diagnostic Code 7114) rated 0% or 20% solely on a normal/calcified Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) when ankle pressure, toe pressure, or TcPO2 testing showed worse circulation under corrected Note (2) (86 FR 62095).

Cold Injury Residuals (Diagnostic Code 7122, from winter combat or training) bundled into one combined percentage instead of separate ratings for each affected hand, foot, ear, or nose (plus the § 4.26 bilateral factor and separate peripheral neuropathy ratings).
important_cautions: Existing pre-November 14, 2021 heart ratings are protected: if you held a running 60% or 100% heart rating based on LVEF before November 14, 2021, VA is strictly prohibited from lowering it simply because the November 14, 2021 schedule removed standalone LVEF (38 U.S.C. § 1155; 38 C.F.R. § 3.951(a)).

Conversely, for initial or increased-rating heart claims filed ON OR AFTER November 14, 2021, standalone LVEF percentages and plain ECG/X-ray hypertrophy are no longer part of the General Rating Formula (30% hypertrophy now requires echocardiogram, multigated acquisition scan, or cardiac MRI).
Do not apply 1998 LVEF/METs criteria to prove Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) in final decisions issued BEFORE January 12, 1998.
Remember 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c): once the Board of Veterans' Appeals issues a final merits decision on a CUE motion for a specific Board issue, no second CUE motion is allowed on that issue.
questions_for_representative: During any rating period between January 12, 1998 and November 13, 2021, did my cardiology records show an ejection fraction (LVEF) of 50% or less, or left ventricular hypertrophy on ECG, X-ray, or echocardiogram?
On my heart exam, were my METs (metabolic equivalents) measured or medically estimated accurately based on when shortness of breath, fatigue, chest pain, or dizziness begins?
If I have diabetes or kidney disease with Peripheral Arterial Disease (Diagnostic Code 7114), did the examiner perform toe pressure or TcPO2 testing instead of relying on calcified ABI numbers?
If I have cold injury residuals (Diagnostic Code 7122), did VA rate each affected hand, foot, ear, and nose separately plus peripheral nerve damage?
